name: Registan Square
description: The heart of ancient Samarkand and the most famous public square in Central Asia, framed by three monumental madrasahs covered in turquoise mosaics.
best_time: Sunset, or early morning to avoid crowds
historical_significance: Surrounded by the Ulugh Beg, Sher-Dor, and Tilya-Kori madrasahs, Registan Square was the commercial and educational center of Timurid Samarkand and remains the city's defining landmark.

name: Gur-e-Amir Mausoleum
description: The mausoleum of Amir Timur (Tamerlane), topped with a fluted turquoise dome and considered a masterpiece of Timurid architecture.
historical_significance: Built as a tomb for Timur's grandson, it later became the resting place of Timur himself and set the architectural template later echoed by the Taj Mahal in India.

name: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
description: One of the largest and once grandest mosques in the Islamic world, commissioned by Timur after his campaign in India.
historical_significance: Named after Timur's senior wife, the mosque was one of the largest in the Islamic world at the time and, though partially ruined by an earthquake, has been substantially restored.

name: Shah-i-Zinda Necropolis
description: A stunning avenue of mausoleums with some of the richest tilework in Central Asia, built up over several centuries.
historical_significance: Built around the (legendary) grave of Qusam ibn Abbas, a cousin of the Prophet Muhammad, this avenue of tombs shows the evolution of Central Asian tile art across 800 years.

name: Ulugh Beg Observatory
description: The remains of a 15th-century astronomical observatory built by the astronomer-king Ulugh Beg, grandson of Timur.
historical_significance: Ulugh Beg used this observatory's giant sextant to catalogue over a thousand stars with remarkable precision for the era, producing tables used across the Islamic world and Europe.

name: Siab Bazaar
description: Samarkand's oldest and largest traditional market, next to Bibi-Khanym Mosque, famous for its bread, dried fruit, and spices.
best_time: Morning, when it's freshest and least crowded
historical_significance: A working market on the old Silk Road trade route, still the best place in the city to see round Samarkand bread being baked and sold.

name: Hazrat Khizr Mosque
description: A hilltop mosque with sweeping views over the Bibi-Khanym Mosque and Siab Bazaar, rebuilt in the 19th century.
historical_significance: One of the oldest mosque sites in Samarkand, associated with the prophet Khizr; the current structure dates mostly from a 19th-century rebuild.

name: Afrosiyob Museum
description: A museum built over the ruins of ancient Afrosiyob, the pre-Mongol city that predates modern Samarkand, with notable wall-painting fragments.
year_built: Founded 1970; site dates to 7th century BCE
historical_significance: Sits above the ruins of Afrosiyob, the original city of Samarkand founded around the 7th century BCE and destroyed by the Mongols in 1220; the museum's Sogdian murals are a highlight.
